findings.title: [P2] Chunk the `IN` query to respect backend parameter limits
findings.body: All distinct IDs are now bound into a single `IN (...)` clause (`src/users.ts:24-25`). Unlike the previous per-ID queries, which were individually below any bind limit, a single very large batch (e.g. a dataloader-style caller with thousands of IDs) will exceed common driver/database parameter limits — SQLite's ~999 bind parameters or PostgreSQL's 65,535 — causing the entire call to fail rather than degrading gracefully. Chunking `uniqueIds` into bounded groups (then concatenating the row sets) preserves the batching win without the hard failure ceiling.

findings.title: [P3] Confirm the forced `null` matches the previous missing-ID contract
findings.body: For a missing ID, the old code propagated exactly what `db.users.find(id)` produced (which for many adapters is `undefined` or a not-found rejection, not `null`). The new code unconditionally coerces missing rows to `null` via `byId.get(id) ?? null` at `src/users.ts:27`. Since the PR description states the goal is "preserving existing contracts," and the adapter's `find` semantics are not visible anywhere in this repo, confirm that `null` really is the established not-found value before merging; if `find` returned `undefined`, callers doing strict `=== undefined` or existence checks will observe a changed contract.

findings.title: [P3] Avoid aliasing the same row object across duplicate IDs
findings.body: With duplicate IDs in the input, every output position now receives the *same* row object from `byId` (`src/users.ts:26-27`). The previous implementation issued a separate `find` per occurrence, and adapters that materialize fresh objects per query returned independent entries. If callers mutate returned rows in place, mutating one duplicate entry now silently mutates the other. Low real-world impact, but a behavioral change worth either documenting or avoiding (e.g. shallow-copying per position) if mutable rows are expected.

findings.title: [P3] Sparse-array input now sends `undefined` into the query
findings.body: `ids: string[]` legally permits sparse arrays (e.g. `new Array<string>(1)`). Previously, `map` skipped the hole and `Promise.all` yielded `undefined` at that position. Now the spread at `src/users.ts:22` materializes the hole as `undefined`, which flows through the `Set` into the `in:` filter at line 25 — many query builders reject `undefined` filter values outright, turning a previously-working call into a total failure (or, at best, changing the slot from `undefined` to `null`). Rare input, but a boundary-behavior change introduced by the spread; a `for` loop or a filter on `!= null` before querying would restore the old tolerance.

findings.title: [P3] Add tests for the new batching, ordering, and null-reconstruction behavior
findings.body: The new semantics — de-duplication before querying, single bulk query, reconstruction in original input order, duplicate-ID preservation, `null` for missing rows, and the empty-input fast path (`src/users.ts:22-27`) — are subtle enough to regress silently, and the repository currently has no test files at all to protect them. Adding coverage for at least order preservation, duplicates, and missing IDs would lock in the behavior this PR establishes.
